validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/SPEC, RE-VERIFIED with a genuine second independent source. The sheet's own citable lead is the Asharq Al-Awsat article (archive.aawsat.com, article=101441&issueno=8558, dated 2002-05-04) already referenced in ResearcherNotes -- fetched and read the full Arabic body: a joint Egyptian-Libyan ministerial delegation meeting in Cairo to start implementing an oil+gas pipeline pair; crude-oil line specifically 'Tobruk -> Alexandria' (طبرق -> الاسكندرية), 620 km total (495 km inside Egypt + ~125 km inside Libya, exact match to LengthKnown=620.00), capacity 150,000 bpd (exact match to Capacity=150,000.00 bpd), 50/50 Egyptian-petroleum-sector/Libyan-NOC ownership of the pipeline-owning JV. I then found and verified a SECOND, genuinely independent source the prior pass had not located: oilegypt.com's 'Cooperation between Egypt and Libya' (7 June 2003, English, live and verified) -- an unrelated outlet, different date, different language, and it is also the source Wikipedia's 'Egypt–Libya relations' article cites for the same claim (checked the live wikitext; Wikipedia itself adds no separate primary source, so it is not counted as a third source, per the one-secondary-source rule). oilegypt.com independently confirms: the JV is the 'Arab Company for Oil & Gas pipeline (Al Tube)', an Egyptian joint-stock company; 'The Libyan crude oil will be transferred to the Egyptian refineries through a pipeline from Tabruk in Libya to Alexandria in Egypt'; Egyptian side = EGPC + GASCO + Petrojet holding 50%, Libyan National Petroleum Institute holding the other 50%; JV capital $100 million. This agrees with aawsat on route, direction, fuel, JV structure, and the 50/50 split -- two independent sources, different years (2002 vs 2003) and languages, confirming this is a real, well-documented proposal, not a hallucination or GEM-only entity. Upgrading Fuel, FuelSource, StartLocation, EndLocation, Operator and Owner to tier=high/independent=true on the strength of this second source. Length (620 km) and Capacity (150,000 bpd) stay medium -- only aawsat gives the actual numbers; oilegypt.com does not repeat them, so no second source confirms the specific figures yet. The gem.wiki page's second citation (thefreelibrary.com, titled 'LIBYA - Chad Oil Pipeline To Cameroon' -- an unrelated Chad/Cameroon pipeline) is almost certainly a mismatched footnote: HTTP 403 at origin, no Wayback capture on record (checked via the CDX API, empty result) -- not used, and not what the sheet's own ResearcherNotes cites (aawsat only).

validity.recommendation: footnote only, no value change recommended -- both sources describe a 3-way Egyptian consortium, not solely EGPC
validity.researcher_notes: ATTRIBUTION nuance on Owner2/Operator, now confirmed by BOTH independent sources rather than one. aawsat states the JV's Egyptian 50% share was itself split three ways -- EGPC, the Egyptian Natural Gas Company (GASCO), and Petroleum Projects Co. (بتروجيت / Petrojet). oilegypt.com (2003) says the same thing in English: 'The Egyptian petroleum sector represented by the Egyptian General Petroleum Corporation (EGPC), GASCO and Petrojet have 50% shares and the Libyan national petroleum institute has 50% shares.' GEM's Owner2='Egyptian General Petroleum Corp' 50% is a reasonable simplification (EGPC is the umbrella state entity) but technically compresses three co-investors into one; GEM's separate Operator field (Petrojet) is directly supported by name in both sources as one of the three Egyptian JV partners -- not explicitly labelled the pipeline's day-to-day 'operator' in either source, but a defensible reading given Petrojet is Egypt's standard EPC/pipeline-construction-and-operations vehicle in comparable rows. Not flagging as a hard error, and now tier=high given two agreeing sources on the consortium structure -- just noting neither source uses the word 'operator', so a future pass could split Owner2/Owner3 out to GASCO and Petrojet if GEM wants the consortium modeled explicitly.

validity.recommendation: ESCALATE TO DISCOVERY / country-note flag -- do not touch this row: a materially DIFFERENT Tobruk-Alexandria oil pipeline proposal surfaced in August 2026 and is a separate candidate, not a revival of P3719
validity.researcher_notes: IMPORTANT CONTEXT, not a defect in P3719's stored values -- re-verified all three URLs by fetching full page text (not just the URL-verifier token check), and correcting one thing about the prior pass's tiering. As of this pass (Aug 2026), Egypt and Libya are reported STUDYING a NEW Tobruk-to-Alexandria crude oil pipeline: Libya Herald (Sami Zaptia, 12 Aug 2026, live, full text confirms) and Pipeline Technology Journal (Daniel Onyango, 10 Aug 2026, live, full text confirms) both report ~800 km, >US$1 billion, following talks between Egyptian PM Mostafa Madbouly and Libyan GNU PM Abdel Hamid Aldabaiba/Dbeibeh -- but BOTH explicitly attribute the story to the same origin: 'a government official who spoke to Asharq Bloomberg on condition of anonymity.' That makes these two NOT independent of each other in the confidence-tier sense (one leaked story, two outlets republishing/paraphrasing it), so I am downgrading this finding from the prior pass's 'high' to 'medium'. The third source, OilPrice.com (Cyril Widdershoven/Blue Water Strategy, 17 Aug 2026, live, full text confirms), is a substantially independent analytical treatment -- adds its own BWS cost/capacity/timeline assessment (capacity 150,000-250,000 bpd likely Phase I, CAPEX $1.3-2.2bn, FID 2027, first oil ~2029-2030) rather than just repeating the leak -- and it is valuable for a different reason: it explicitly compares the new project to the OLD one and INDEPENDENTLY confirms this row's own historical numbers ('In 2002... the total pipeline was expected to be 620 km and was initially designed for 150,000 bpd... The Arab Company for Oil and Gas Lines, a 50:50 JV between Libya's NOC and Egypt's EGPC/GASCO'), which is a third, later, analyst-sourced corroboration of P3719's own Length/Capacity/Owner values, independent of both aawsat and oilegypt.com. Net read: the new 2026 initiative shares the corridor and name of P3719's 2002 proposal but differs materially -- 800 km vs 620 km, no fixed capacity vs a fixed 150,000 bpd, GNU-era Libyan government vs the pre-2011 Gaddafi-era NOC, and OilPrice explicitly frames it as 'the resurrection and substantial enlargement of an old one', i.e. a new initiative, not a technical revival of the same project. RECOMMENDATION: P3719 itself should stay as-is (Status=cancelled correctly describes the dead 2002-2006 proposal; ShelvedCancelledType=inferred is already correctly set with no fabricated date-source -- neither ShelvedYear=2004 nor CancelledYear=2006 has any independent source, and none should be fabricated). The 2026 talks are a strong Discovery-candidate for a NEW ProjectID once/if a firmer agreement or FID is reported -- flag in the country note so a future Discovery pass on Egypt/Libya oil doesn't miss it, and so nobody accidentally 'un-cancels' P3719 by conflating the two.

summary: P3719 (Tobruk-Alexandria Oil Pipeline, 2002, cancelled) is a real, correctly-classified 2002-2003 EGPC/Libyan-NOC proposal, now confirmed by TWO independent sources (Asharq Al-Awsat 2002 Arabic + oilegypt.com 2003 English) on route, fuel, JV structure and 50/50 ownership (tier high on 6 fields); Length/Capacity stay medium since only the 2002 article gives the actual numbers. No existence/classification/duplicate defect. Flagged: (1) ShelvedYear/CancelledYear correctly stay UNRESOLVED/inferred -- no source dates the cancellation itself; (2) an attribution nuance, now doubly confirmed -- both sources describe a 3-way Egyptian consortium (EGPC/GASCO/Petrojet) behind the 'Egyptian General Petroleum Corp' 50% share; (3) IMPORTANT, re-verified and re-tiered -- independent, non-GEM reporting from August 2026 (Libya Herald, Pipeline Technology Journal, OilPrice.com, all live-checked) shows Egypt and Libya reviving talks on a NEW, larger Tobruk-Alexandria oil pipeline (~800 km, >$1B, capacity not yet fixed) -- downgraded from a prior draft's 'high' to 'medium' tier because two of the three outlets trace to one Asharq Bloomberg anonymous-official leak; still a materially different project from this 620 km/150,000 bpd/2002 row and a Discovery-candidate escalation, not a change to P3719.
